element.name: Warrior of the Sun
element.source: Warrior of the Sun (Variant) — D&D Wiki

description.p: Was your warrior cast out of their homeland because others envied their power? Did the strength of the sun accidentally cause them to harm a loved one, or are they admired as a hero?
Quick Build. Strength should be your highest ability score, followed by Constitution. The source suggests the Outcast background and a greataxe and chain mail.

ul.li: Hit Dice: 1d12 per Warrior of the Sun level
Hit Points at 1st Level: 12 + your Constitution modifier
Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d12 (or 7) + your Constitution modifier per level after 1st
Tools: "Bewers Supplies" (source spelling; interpreted as brewer's supplies for the proficiency entry)
(a) any martial weapon or (b) any simple weapon
(a) an adventurer's pack or (b) a dungeoneer's pack
Glasses to nullify the effects of sunshine

tr.td: Path of the Sun, Prideful Strike

setters.set: A warrior whose physical might grows with the power of the sun.

element.name: Sunshine
element.source: Warrior of the Sun (Variant) — D&D Wiki

description.p: While it is daytime or you are in sunlight, you gain the benefits below: advantage on Strength and Dexterity checks; a +2d4 bonus to damage rolls (the damage dice increase one size for every 2 levels in this class, to a maximum of 2d12); your unarmed strikes deal 1d10 damage; advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks; advantage on saving throws against being frightened; and the ability to see normally in magical and nonmagical darkness out to 120 feet. Intense Pride: while not under Sunshine, you have disadvantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks and saving throws against being frightened.

element.name: Magic Sense
element.source: Warrior of the Sun (Variant) — D&D Wiki

description.p: Choose one creature within 60 feet. You learn whether its Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution are higher or lower than yours, and its highest-level spell slot, if any. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier and regain all uses after a long rest.

element.name: Blazing Defense
element.source: Warrior of the Sun (Variant) — D&D Wiki

description.p: While Sunshine is active, your AC can be 10 + your Strength modifier + your Constitution modifier. If you are wearing armor, choose whether to use its AC or this AC. You can still use magical properties of armor while using this feature. You are immune to the effects of extreme cold and extreme heat, even when Sunshine is inactive.

element.source: Warrior of the Sun (Variant) — D&D Wiki

description.p: When Sunshine is not active, you can use a bonus action to transform and gain Sunshine for 2 minutes. When the transformation ends, choose to expend one Hit Die or suffer one level of exhaustion.

element.name: Path of the Sun
element.source: Warrior of the Sun (Variant) — D&D Wiki

description.p: Choose the Sun of Strength or Sun of Skill path. Your path grants features at 3rd, 7th, 11th, 15th, and 18th level.

element.name: Prideful Strike
element.source: Warrior of the Sun (Variant) — D&D Wiki

description.p: While Sunshine is active, use a bonus action to make a powerful strike in a line 5 feet wide. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier). On a failed save, it takes bludgeoning damage; the source text gives 2d10 + your Strength modifier, or half damage on a failed save. Objects and structures that are not worn or carried take maximum damage. Damage increases to 3d10 at 5th level, 5d10 at 11th level, and 7d10 at 17th level. The line is 10 feet long, increasing to 20 feet at 9th level and 30 feet at 17th level. Note: the source text says half damage on a failed save; this appears internally inconsistent and is preserved for DM adjudication.

element.source: Warrior of the Sun (Variant) — D&D Wiki

description.p: When you take fire or radiant damage, you instead absorb it and regain hit points equal to all the damage you would have taken.

element.name: Sun's Blessing
element.source: Warrior of the Sun (Variant) — D&D Wiki

description.p: When an effect allows you to make a Constitution saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage on a success and half damage on a failure. Your hit point maximum also increases by 3 times your level. Whenever you gain a level thereafter, your hit point maximum increases by an additional 3 hit points.

element.name: Godly Radiance
element.source: Warrior of the Sun (Variant) — D&D Wiki

description.p: While Sunshine is active, when you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it and must use the new roll. You can do so once per long rest; this increases to twice per long rest at 13th level and three times per long rest at 17th level.

element.source: Warrior of the Sun (Variant) — D&D Wiki

element.name: Cruel Sun
element.source: Warrior of the Sun (Variant) — D&D Wiki

description.p: As a bonus action while Sunshine is active, summon a blazing fireball that floats around you. While active, you gain +2 AC; nonmagical metal within 10 feet (excluding your own) melts and is affected as though by heat metal; it emits bright light for 60 feet and dim light for another 60 feet, and dispels magical darkness in its bright light (except in The One or The One: Ultimate forms). You can shoot it at a visible target within 30 feet: the target makes a Dexterity save (DC = 8 + proficiency bonus + Strength modifier), taking 5d10 fire + 4d8 radiant + your Strength modifier damage and being pushed 10 feet on a failure, or half damage without push on a success. Alternatively, ride it and gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed. Uses equal your Strength modifier; regain all uses after a short or long rest.

element.name: The One
element.source: Warrior of the Sun (Variant) — D&D Wiki

description.p: As an action, enter this form for 1 minute; once used, regain the ability after a long rest. You gain bonus hit points equal to proficiency bonus × class level; resistance to all damage; immunity to prone, grappled, blinded, possessed, poisoned, stunned, paralyzed, restrained, and petrified; a 10-foot aura that deals fire damage equal to your Charisma modifier to creatures in it at the start of your turns; and your damage ignores resistance, immunity, and absorption. At the end, you suffer 1 level of exhaustion.

element.name: The Ultimate One
element.source: Warrior of the Sun (Variant) — D&D Wiki

description.p: Under the same conditions as The One, you can enter this form for 1 minute. You gain temporary hit points equal to your hit point maximum; all damage you deal increases by your proficiency bonus plus your class level; and your aura increases to 30 feet and deals 10d10 fire damage to all creatures within it. At the end, you suffer 5 levels of exhaustion and are reduced to 1 hit point.

element.name: Divine Axe Rhitta
element.source: Warrior of the Sun (Variant) — D&D Wiki

description.p: You gain a massive golden one-handed battleaxe that only you can lift or wield, and only while Sunshine is active. As a bonus action, call it to your hand from any distance; if it is on another plane, it takes 2 rounds to arrive. It grants +4 to attack and damage rolls and deals 1d12 + Strength modifier slashing damage plus 3d6 radiant or fire damage per hit; its damage is magical and silvered for overcoming resistance and immunity, and your speed increases by 10 feet while wielding it. At 20th level, you may attune to it; its slashing damage becomes 2d12 + Strength modifier, but it uses one of your normal magic-item attunement slots. If lost or destroyed, a 1-minute ritual at noon resummons it. The ritual can also copy the magical abilities of one other magic weapon at a time. You can suppress your Intense Aura around the axe while wielding it. You know the light cantrip and can cast daylight a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining uses after a long rest.

description.p: You can share Sunshine with another creature. If you do, you lose Sunshine and all features the class grants from it. Sunshine returns after that creature dies or after one long rest. When Sunshine returns, the other creature loses 1 point of Constitution.

element.source: Warrior of the Sun (Variant) — D&D Wiki

description.p: While in The One or The One: Ultimate form, use an action to thrust your finger at an opponent. The target makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 27). On a failure, it takes 20d6 radiant damage, is pushed 100 feet, and is knocked prone. On a success, it takes half damage and is not pushed. The source adds: 'Rather fail or success the damage is still doubled or tripled respectively.' This unclear final clause is preserved for DM adjudication.
